findings.issue: Fortune 'This week had one of the incredible vaults...' is a weekly-wrap style headline stamped 24 Feb 08:00 that may describe the full week and appear after the cutoff; it was used to describe the 24 Feb reversal.
findings.resolution: Sentence removed; reversal remains supported by card closes and n1126.

findings.issue: Uncited statement of what 'investors read' and a Fed-path inference presented as fact.
Commentary headline only says bond market sends flawed signals; sentence asserted labour data and long-yield growth pricing beyond the headline.
findings.resolution: Trimmed to what the headline supports.

findings.location: crypto New / Most Important; earnings_pattern Pattern; catalysts Coinbase (n0678, n0679)
findings.issue: Coinbase results timing relative to the 24 Feb US close is unclear; juxtaposing the +3.95% close with the beat and calling it an archetype of a muted reaction implied a reaction not evidenced.
findings.resolution: Close stated as possibly not reflecting the report; Pattern sentence reframed as an open forward question.

findings.issue: MP Materials results timing unclear; 'and the shares closed up 7.37%' implied a reaction to the report.
findings.resolution: Reworded to a separate session move; also removed unsupported 'largest supply-risk premium' claim.

findings.issue: Claimed the war 'lowered expected policy rates and raised security spending' without headline support.
findings.resolution: Reworded to yields lower and cyber defence in focus; hedged yield causation.

findings.issue: Fed note on bank business-loan supply was claimed to show where a March hike would show up.

Unsupported causal or flow claims: rotation 'funded out of energy', staples fell because of input costs, collateral strain for generators, Asian vs US chip split attributed to investor views on sanctions.
findings.resolution: Replaced with rotation/timing language and hedged mechanisms; trading-down line softened.

findings.issue: EWJ move interpreted as foreign holders' view.
Interpretation beyond headline (losses landing on concentrated holders not cascading; Alibaba 'concedes' domestic core maturing; rust-belt plan 'signals' local support demand).
Refugee burden 'falling most heavily on Poland', Parkiet framing of NBP choice, and 'local attention migrating' went beyond headlines.
Overreach: 'leverage migrating on-chain', Deere 'paid for', Wayfair 'de-rating'.

Numbers, session dates, source tags, curve wording (positively sloped, bear flattening), 20/5/1-session horizons and period names (FB, RTX, Mercedes-Benz Group, RIOT) checked against the card; no numeric spot-FX, no post-cutoff events (EU second package, UN vote, Putin sanctions, PCE, 25 Feb ASX) found. No discrepancies found.

scope_limits: Own-date feed and card only; headlines not article bodies, so claims limited to headline content. Day-granular 08:00 stamps mean intraday and overnight timing of some 24 Feb items cannot be verified. Verifier reports 0 warnings after edits.

recommended_exclusions.reason: Fortune weekly-wrap style headline ('This week had one of the incredible vaults') stamped 24 Feb but likely written after the 24 Feb close or the week's end; possibly after cutoff. Removed from draft.
ABC report of the ASX rebound after the $74b wipe-out describes the 25 Feb ASX session, after the cutoff; misdated to 24 Feb.
Reuters 'Investors regain risk appetite; dollar, oil pare gains after Ukraine invasion' is likely an Asian Friday wrap after the cutoff; misdated to 24 Feb.
NPR 'Russia invades Ukraine as explosions are heard in Kyiv' stamped 23 Feb 08:00, before the invasion began (about 03:00 UTC 24 Feb); misdated.
marketscreener.com rolling 'Agriculture: Stock prices and news' page stamped 24 Feb 23:35 UTC; live/rolling page, not a dated headline.
